topic: How does the hierarchical classification framework impact satellite link budget margins when prioritizing QoS-sensitive traffic?
consensus_response: The hierarchical classification framework impacts satellite link budget margins by prioritizing QoS-sensitive traffic based on latency requirements. Current frameworks, such as Diffserv and MPLS, focus on managing available capacity and neglect high fixed latencies on links, leading to inefficient resource allocation and reduced accuracy in classifying and prioritizing traffic. This oversight compromises QoE for end-users and reduces the overall efficiency of resource utilization. Network slicing techniques can provide more granular control over resource allocation and consider both capacity and latency requirements to optimize satellite link budget margins.
reference_context: The reference context highlights limitations of current hierarchical classification frameworks, such as Diffserv, MPLS, QoS-OSPF with RSVP, DVB-S2/RCS2, LTE, ECMP, and WiBACK techniques, in managing high fixed latencies on satellite links. These approaches focus on managing available capacity rather than link characteristics like latency and jitter.
